display.title: Episode 163: Shoot Bullets in the Jacket Too
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi teaches the third of the Twelve Pesukim, Bechol Dor Vador, and tells how a poor tzedakah collector outsmarted an armed robber to save the money for the poor.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi continues marching through the Twelve Pesukim with number three, Bechol Dor Vador: in every generation each Jew should feel as if he himself left Egypt, and thank Hashem for it. The Hakochainik march sings the pasuk, followed by news of an illustrated Twelve Pesukim booklet and a sponsor message. Uncle Yossi explains how Tzivos Hashem members earn points and rise in rank, from private all the way to general, by writing in what they learned and completing mitzvah missions, and wishes several listeners a happy birthday. A young yeshiva student reads from the Chumash and leads the Shema. Story time tells of Rebbe Nachman, a woodcutter who distributed the town's tzedakah. When a robber takes the tzedakah money at gunpoint, Rebbe Nachman asks him to shoot holes in his jacket and hat as proof, until the gun is empty; then he grabs back the money and the robber flees. Shlomo HaMelech's words that tzedakah saves from death close the story. In Mitzvah Time, a listener answers questions about last week's story of the butcher who cared for his parents.
display.lesson: Tzedakah is so great that it can save a person's life, and money given for the poor must be guarded even more carefully than your own.

date.note: Week before ep. 164 ('tomorrow night is Rosh Chodesh Adar' = 19 Feb 1985); Yud Shevat birthday already past; ep. 162 was the Tu B'Shvat show. Weekly estimate was 3 weeks late.

advisories.note: A robber holds up the tzedakah collector at gunpoint, threatens his life and fires shots into his jacket and hat; no one is hurt.

privacy.note: Birthday children, the Shema guest and the Mitzvah Time quiz winner are named in full.
